name: Cassava Leaf Spot (Brown Leaf Spot)
description: A fungal disease causing brown spots on cassava leaves, leading to premature defoliation. It is widespread in cassava-growing regions and can cause significant yield reduction when infections are severe.
symptoms: Circular to irregular brown spots on older leaves
Spots with dark brown margins and lighter centers
Premature leaf drop starting from lower leaves
Severe defoliation exposing stems and reducing root bulking
causes: Cercospora henningsii and Cercospora vicosae fungi
Warm, humid weather favoring spore production
Dense plantings with poor air circulation
Continuous cassava cultivation in same field
Fungal survival on crop debris between seasons
treatments: Apply copper-based fungicides or mancozeb at first symptoms
Spray benomyl or thiophanate-methyl for systemic control
Remove and destroy heavily infected leaves
prevention: Space plants adequately for air circulation
Remove and destroy crop debris after harvest
Remove volunteer cassava plants between seasons
